HEXACO responses generated by six language models

Source: R/data.R
hexaco_llm.Rd

89,597 synthetic respondents to the 240 IPIP-HEXACO items, generated by six large language models for Canada, Great Britain and the United States, in 10 independent attempts of about 500 respondents per model and country. They pair with the real answers in hexaco_real.

Usage

hexaco_llm

Format

A data frame with 89,597 rows (one per synthetic respondent) and 243 columns: model (factor, the six models above), country (factor: Canada, Great Britain or United States), attempt (1 to 10) and the 240 items, named as in hexaco_items$item.

Source

Generated by Okan Bulut. The script is data-raw/hexaco.R in the package's GitHub repository.

Details

Each respondent was generated in its own conversation. The model was asked to simulate one adult drawn at random from the general adult population of the named country (not an average or typical person), to answer as that person rather than as an AI or a socially desirable person, and to use the full range of the scale. No demographic details were given, so the country was the only part of the prompt that changed. The items were shown in their original order in six blocks of 40, at temperature 1.0.

modelCheckpoint or model IDDeveloperGenerated
Gemma 4 26Bgoogle/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it (FP8)GoogleJuly to September 2026
GPT-OSS-120Bopenai/gpt-oss-120b (MXFP4)OpenAIJuly to September 2026
Qwen 3.8 27BQwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8AlibabaJuly to September 2026
Qwen 3.5 122BQwen/Qwen3.5-122B-A10B-FP8AlibabaJuly to September 2026
Claude Haiku 5.5claude-haiku-5-5AnthropicNovember 2026
GPT-4.1 minigpt-4.1-miniOpenAINovember 2026

The four open-weight models ran on the Aleph Inference Gateway of the Vulcan cluster (Digital Research Alliance of Canada). Claude Haiku 5.5 ran through the Anthropic API at its default temperature (1.0) with thinking turned off; that API takes no sampling seed. GPT-4.1 mini is the model ID logged in the files that were supplied for ChatGPT.

Rows logged under another model were removed: 379 rows in the Qwen 3.8 27B files and 11 rows (logged as gpt-4o-2024-08-06) in the GPT-4.1 mini files. One GPT-4.1 mini attempt for the United States has 497 respondents. So a few attempts have fewer than 500 respondents. As in hexaco_real, answers are stored as given (1 to 7), with reverse-keyed items not reversed. No answer is missing.

See also

hexaco_real, hexaco_items, synthetic_coverage(), authenticity_benchmark() and the article Checking synthetic respondents.

Examples

with(hexaco_llm, table(model, country))
#>                   country
#> model              Canada Great Britain United States
#>   Gemma 4 26B        5000          5000          5000
#>   GPT-OSS-120B       5000          5000          5000
#>   Qwen 3.8 27B       4945          4995          4671
#>   Qwen 3.5 122B      5000          5000          5000
#>   Claude Haiku 5.5   5000          5000          5000
#>   GPT-4.1 mini       5000          5000          4986
# one list per model, one data frame per attempt: the shape that
# synthetic_coverage() and authenticity_benchmark() take
h <- hexaco_items$item[hexaco_items$trait == "H"]
ca <- hexaco_llm[hexaco_llm$country == "Canada", ]
syn <- lapply(split(ca, ca$model), function(m) split(m[h], m$attempt))
lengths(syn)
#>      Gemma 4 26B     GPT-OSS-120B     Qwen 3.8 27B    Qwen 3.5 122B 
#>               10               10               10               10 
#> Claude Haiku 5.5     GPT-4.1 mini 
#>               10               10
